facts.rationale: The active initializer installs the four-laser accessory callback, while this phase's physics wrapper applies shared animation-translation velocity.
facts.value: Supplies animation-driven movement for the active four-laser phase of Crazy Hand's sequence behaviorally identified as Laser Nail. The Poke1 code label is not evidence of the separate Tri-Poke mechanic.

evidence.why: Four-laser lifecycle and final animation handoff.

facts.rationale: The preceding active phase creates four laser items and requests their shutdown when entering 0x168; this callback handles that ending state's completion.
facts.value: Handles animation completion of the ending phase of Crazy Hand's four-laser sequence, behaviorally identified as Laser Nail, and hands control to shared post-action positioning setup. Its Poke2 label does not establish a third physical poke.

evidence.why: Latch producer/consumer, retained handles and ordered normal cleanup.
Deferred request flag, reset branch and subsequent destruction test.
External cleanup consumer for the same item and audio slots.

facts.rationale: Preserves the exact normal cleanup order, distinguishes pointer clearing from object destruction, and records the external handle consumer without assuming all interruption paths are covered.
facts.value: Entry to 0x167 installs an accessory callback and arms cmd_vars[0]. The callback consumes any nonzero latch to create four attached laser items, storing pointers in mv.ch.grab.x28/x2C/x30/x34, and three audio results in mv.ch.unk0.x38/x3C/x40, then clears the latch. On active-animation exhaustion, the 0x168 initializer first keys off the voices and resets their slots to -1; the returning active animation callback then requests item shutdown and clears the four fighter-held pointers. Item shutdown is deferred to item-side processing, whose animation-reset branch can clear the request flag before its test. The same handles also have a cross-file cleanup consumer in ftCh_GrabUnk1_8015ADD0.
